doc_verification.detail: Filter parameter is documented as optional object for search endpoint. Docs at https://api.qdrant.tech/api-reference/points/search-points specify filter with nested conditions (must/should/must_not) and operators (match/range/nested/is_empty/etc). Version 1.19.x matches target v1.18.2 (major.minor). Contract qdrant_type_search_points_001 asserts vector dimension constraints, not filter validation.

execution_evidence.log_pattern: INFO: Empty filter accepted → INFO: Null filter accepted → Error quality for array filter: 2/3 (raw=Format error in JSON body: invalid length 1, expected struct Filter with 4 elements) → Error quality for invalid operator: 1/3 (raw=Expected some form of condition) → Error quality for string range: 0/3 (raw='10' does not match accepted datetime format RFC3339) → INFO: Valid filter correctly returned 2 results → DEFECT_FOUND (Type2_PoorDiagnostics) — Invalid operator error lacks details (score 1/3)
secondary_observations: Array filter error provides partial context (score 2/3)

http_semantics.note: Invalid filter structures return HTTP 200 with error status field, not 4xx. For example: {"status":{"error":"Format error in JSON body: invalid length 1, expected struct Filter with 4 elements at line 1 column 679"},"time":0.0}

contract_grounding.note: Contract constraint only covers vector dimension matching, not filter structure validation. Filter validation defects fall outside this constraint's scope.

chain_links: script:semantic_points_search_filter_nested_001.py (sent empty filter, null filter, array-as-filter, invalid operator, invalid range)
log:Empty/null accepted (200), array rejected with partial error msg (2/3), invalid operator rejected with vague error (1/3), string range rejected with misleading error (0/3)

source_grounding.source_excerpt: Filter struct at lib/segment/src/types.rs:3834-3866 defines Filter with should/must/must_not fields using #[validate(nested)]. Each field is Option<Vec<Condition>> with serde(default). Validation relies on validator crate's Validate trait. Missing field error 'missing field `ids`' originates in REST API conversion layer when PointsSelector expects either point_ids or filter but receives ambiguous compound filter. Error message generated by serde deserialization, not by custom validation logic.
source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST request → actix update_api.rs:delete_points() → Json<PointsSelector> deserialization → serde validates Filter → validator::Validate nested validation → operation processing. Error messages come from serde, not domain-specific validation, explaining poor diagnostic quality.

mundane_explanation.surviving: Type2_PoorDiagnostics confirmed — filter validation error messages lack actionable details (invalid operator: 'Expected some form of condition' without specifying which operator/field, string range: datetime format error when expecting number range). Empty/null filters silently accepted despite being nonsensical for search operations.
